A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Nadaraya–Watson interpolation study. Their text, equations, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison: Appendices A–D are retained, and v3 adds Appendix E.

before.justification: Section 5 reports original simulations on one-dimensional mixture and spherical data, including classification-error curves across exponents, label-noise levels, and sample sizes in Figures 3 and 4.

after.justification: Section 6 retains the original simulations and adds MNIST classification results in Figure 5. Appendix E reports an additional Gaussian input-noise experiment in Figure 6.

M1.justification: Equation (1) retains the same inverse-distance-weighted binary classifier and interpolation rule. The added experiments apply this existing method; corrections in the proof sketch do not change its procedure.

E1.justification: v2 evaluates only synthetic one-dimensional and spherical distributions. v3 adds MNIST handwritten-digit 0/1 classification and Gaussian-corrupted spherical inputs, substantially extending coverage to real images and departures from an ideal manifold.

E2.justification: Neither version empirically evaluates competing algorithms against NW. The curves vary NW parameters and data conditions; k-nearest neighbors remains a theoretical comparison, and the new intrinsic-dimension citation is not an evaluated classifier baseline.

E3.justification: Existing synthetic protocols are retained. New MNIST sweeps use all 12,665 training examples while varying label noise, or fix p = 0.1 while varying sample size. Appendix E adds a Gaussian-variance sweep with m = 2000 and p = 0.04, extending the existing evaluation design.

E4.justification: Appendix E adds a focused robustness analysis: independent Gaussian perturbations move spherical inputs away from the manifold, testing how the error-minimizing exponent changes with input-noise variance. This analysis and Figure 6 are absent from v2.

E5.justification: Both experiment sections state that each experiment was run 50 times and report mean errors with 95% confidence intervals. The additional plots retain this reporting practice; no changed run count or statistical procedure is documented.

E6.justification: Figures 3 and 4 retain identical plotted results. v3 substantially expands the empirical findings with MNIST error curves, including an optimum near β = 8 at p = 0.1, and input-noise results showing the preferred β shifting from about 2 toward 3; at variance 0.04 it is approximately 2.5.

T1.justification: v3 restricts the general noise setting and introductory theorem statements from p < 1/2 to p < 0.49, and explicitly applies this range to the tempered theorem. Its proof sketch corrects inverse-distance powers, including a missing β exponent. The detailed proofs in Appendices A–D are otherwise substantively retained.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion retain the overfitting trichotomy and dimension-tuning message. However, the informal main result in Theorem 1.2 narrows its noise-range claim to p < 0.49, aligning it with the catastrophic-overfitting theorem, which already had that restriction in v2.

C2.justification: v3 adds suggested applicability to smoothly varying label noise and a broader interpretation of the catastrophic construction. It relates the MNIST optimum to intrinsic dimension and interprets the Gaussian experiment as robustness evidence, explicitly acknowledging that input noise is outside the current formal results.

D1.justification: New Appendix E documents an explicit data-generation recipe: sample spherical points according to Equation (5), then independently add Gaussian perturbations with covariance σ²I3. This supplies reproducibility information for the added robustness experiment.

R1.justification: v3 adds Pope et al. (2021) to contextualize the MNIST intrinsic-dimension finding. Related work also distinguishes the paper's locality-based proofs from spectral analyses and their additional assumptions. The central novelty claim was already present in v2.

P1.justification: Related work becomes Section 2 instead of Subsection 1.1, with subsequent sections renumbered. Experiments gain synthetic-data and MNIST subsections, and Appendix E is added. Most existing prose is retained, with limited explanatory insertions and corrections.

P2.justification: v3 adds the two-panel MNIST Figure 5 and the input-noise Figure 6. Original figures are retained; Figure 3 moves from PDF page 10 to page 11, with accompanying text and page reflow. The overall visual format remains stable.

improvement.justification: The MNIST and Gaussian-noise experiments broaden support for the tuning interpretation beyond idealized synthetic data. Aligning the introductory noise range with the existing catastrophic theorem and correcting proof-sketch exponents improve precision. These are useful but limited gains: the central mathematical arguments and unproved manifold extension remain essentially unchanged.
